fields.hero_description: Describe your practice. Emergent builds the Botox consent form with your risk statements and screening questions, then keeps every signed visit on the patient's record.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Botox Consent Record
fields.features_subheading: The pieces an injector checks before the first injection, and the ones the front desk looks up afterward.
fields.feature_1:
The Medication Guide as page one

Attach the Medication Guide for the product you inject as the first screen. Patients read it before any consent question appears, and the record notes when they opened it.
fields.feature_2:
Risks initialed one at a time

Write each risk your injector discusses as its own statement with an initials box. A patient who skips one cannot reach the signature, and every initial stays with the form.
fields.feature_3:
Screening questions your injector writes

Ask what your injector needs answered before treating anyone, like a new prescription. Any yes moves that form onto the injector's review list ahead of the appointment.
fields.feature_4:
Product and lot number on the record

Record the product and the vial's lot number after the injections. Units of one toxin product do not convert to another's, and naming the product keeps the chart clear.
fields.feature_5:
A signed form for every visit

Ask returning patients to confirm their earlier answers and sign again. Each visit keeps its own dated consent, and the front desk opens a patient's whole history from one search.
fields.feature_6:
Code your practice can take with it

Export the full source code to your GitHub on paid plans. A developer can run the consent form inside your own booking site or patient portal and keep changing it from there.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Practices Run Botox Consent
fields.tab_content_1:
Any yes on screening goes to the injector's review list

Juniper Aesthetics sends the consent link 24 hours before each neurotoxin appointment, with the Medication Guide as the first page. Patients answer nurse injector Ana Cruz's screening questions, then initial each risk. A yes to any question puts that form on her review list, and she calls the patient before the visit.
fields.tab_content_2:
The vial's lot number sits beside the patient's signature

Dr. Nadia Okafor offers neurotoxin treatment at Harbor Dental. Patients sign on the front-desk tablet, and the form is open in the operatory when they sit down. After the injections she adds the product, the areas treated and the lot number from the vial, all on the record that holds the signature.
fields.tab_content_3:
Fourth visit, fourth signature, no retyping

When a returning patient books at Cedar Skin Clinic, her form opens with last visit's answers filled in. Mia Torres confirms her medications, updates her phone number and signs again. Her record now holds four signed consents, one per visit and each dated, and the injector sees what changed since the last one.
fields.tab_content_4:
Only photos cleared for marketing reach the gallery

Photo consent at Cedar Skin Clinic is a separate screen with two choices: chart only, or chart and marketing. Photos taken at the visit carry the patient's choice. This month, 9 of 40 patients chose marketing, and the gallery the marketing team uses shows only their photos.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Botox Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work happens before the builder opens: deciding what your injector tells patients and what they need to hear back.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the Medication Guide up front
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give each risk its own line
fields.howto_step_1_des: Sit with your injector and write down what they tell every patient before a neurotoxin treatment: what the injection does, the risks they mention and the alternatives, including no treatment at all. The form exists to record that conversation.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Botox Cosmetic comes with an FDA Medication Guide written for patients. Place it, or the guide for whichever product you stock, on the first screen. Patients read it before any question appears, and the record shows when they opened it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write every risk your injector covers as a separate sentence, in the words the injector uses out loud. Clinical terms are hard to read on a phone screen. The signature box stays locked until the patient has initialed each one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide what your injector has to know before treating anyone, for example a new prescription or a recent procedure. Pick which answers send the form to the injector for review, and who receives the alert when one arrives before an appointment.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your consent wording and screening questions. Emergent builds the form with its review list, plus a table of signed records. Ask for changes in plain English, such as a Spanish version or a screen for photo consent.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect it to your booking flow
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the consent link with each appointment confirmation and email patients a PDF of what they signed. Emergent connects to any tool with an API, including the booking or practice management software your front desk already runs.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it, then have it reviewed
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign the form yourself twice, once with a yes on screening and once without, then open both records. Ask your medical director and a healthcare attorney to read the wording before the first patient signs, because consent rules differ by state.
